images.author: Coke Smith
images.why: Standing individual with prominent horns and chestnut-and-white markings. Caption explicitly identifies wild lowland bongo, Tragelaphus eurycerus eurycerus, at Dzanga Bai, CAR. Native resolution and download unverified.

images.author: Coke Smith
images.why: Walking individual in a natural muddy clearing; conspicuous spiral horns and striped coat. Source confirms wild lowland bongo at Dzanga Bai, CAR. Native resolution and download unverified.

images.author: Coke Smith
images.why: Alternative walking pose with long horns and visible stripes against subdued wetland surroundings. Caption confirms wild lowland bongo, CAR. Native resolution and download unverified.

images.author: Coke Smith
images.why: Solitary, alert bongo beside a fallen log; strong facial markings and natural habitat context. Caption confirms the western/lowland subspecies at Dzanga Bai. Native resolution and download unverified.

images.author: Miguel Bellosta
images.why: Official protected-area photograph captioned as a bongo in Dzanga-Sangha; accompanying text explicitly identifies western bongo. Strong geographic match for Central Africa. Native resolution and download unverified.

images.author: Coke Smith
images.why: Wild lowland bongos at a waterhole, with rich coat colour and horned adults. Group-composition fallback; a 9:10 crop would need careful subject selection. Native resolution and download unverified.

images.author: Nuria Ortega
images.why: Official photograph captioned 'Bongo Antelopes' within the western-bongo section. Authentic Central African habitat alternative. Native dimensions and suitability for a tight individual crop remain unverified.

images.author: Paul Carter
images.why: Caption identifies Bongo, Tragelaphus eurycerus, at Dzanga Bai, photographed March 2025. Wild group fallback; linked rendition is only 845×437, below the preferred resolution.

images.author: Roberta Kravette
images.why: Solitary mountain zebra in warm morning light among golden grasses at Palmwag, Namibia. Source caption explicitly identifies mountain zebra. Native resolution and download unverified.

images.author: unknown
images.why: Living, alert individual in sunlit grass and scrub. Page identifies the local animals as Hartmann's mountain zebras at Ondjou Wilderness Reserve. URL requests 2500×1875; native resolution and download unverified.

images.author: Cliff and Suretha Dorse
images.why: Conservation-source photograph explicitly identified as Equus zebra hartmannae, with Namib-Naukluft locality in the image filename. Strong species provenance. Native resolution and download unverified.

images.author: unknown
images.why: Full-body running stallion on an open Namibian plain; an energetic poster alternative. Source identifies Hartmann's mountain zebra and labels this photograph as a stallion. Native resolution and download unverified.

images.author: Colin Watts
images.why: Freely licensed wild group photograph explicitly captioned 'A group of mountain Zebra in Namibia.' Offers habitat context; less suited to an isolated-animal crop. 3000px delivery requested; native dimensions unverified.

images.author: Morris Gosling
images.why: Three Hartmann's mountain zebras on rocky terrain with distant hills and clear sky. Caption confirms Gondwana Canyon Park, Namibia. Group-composition fallback; native resolution unverified.

images.author: Badufle Paulin
images.why: Alert solitary animal facing the camera amid golden grass and low hills. Caption explicitly names Hartmann's zebra in Namibia. Attractive composition, but this 1280px rendition falls below the preferred resolution.

images.author: Paul van Schalkwyk
images.why: Photographer-credited image on a species-specific page identifying Equus zebra hartmannae and its diagnostic white belly and dewlap. Species-confirmed alternative; composition, native resolution and download remain unverified.
